title: WBC heavyweight champions, 1963 onward
hook: Who has held the WBC heavyweight title the longest?
caveat: One sanctioning body's title, not the lineal or undisputed championship: WBC reigns can begin by promotion of a contender or end by stripping, and other bodies' champions held rival belts at the same time.

source.name: Wikipedia: List of WBC world champions (Heavyweight table), via MediaWiki API
source.terms: Wikipedia text is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution + share-alike); reuse of this derived data must credit Wikipedia contributors and carry the same licence.
source.notes: Reigns overlapping 1963-2025. Dates as the table gives them; month-only dates are set to the 1st with fromPrecision 'month'. A reign with no note in the table is taken to begin by beating the previous champion when the previous reign ended that same day. 'to: null' means current at revid 1378619788; series counts its days to 2025-12-31. Cross-check: 31/31 reign start dates also appear verbatim in 'List of world heavyweight boxing champions' (revid 1374895974); not found there: none (left as the WBC list gives them).

vacancies.reason: Ali was stripped of the title due to being suspended for refusing to be inducted in the U.S. Army.
Holmes vacated the title after a dispute with his promoter Don King over the proposed purse for a fight against mandatory challenger Greg Page.
Tyson vacated the title to pursue a bout against Evander Holyfield instead of mandatory challenger Lennox Lewis.
Lewis retired as champion and chose not to rematch Vitali Klitschko ahead of a WBC-mandated 1 March deadline to accept the bout.
Klitschko vacated the title to focus on his career in politics in Ukraine.

events.text: Title vacant: Ali was stripped of the title due to being suspended for refusing to be inducted in the U.S.
Muhammad Ali regains the title (def. George Foreman)
Larry Holmes begins the reign with the most defenses in this span (16)
Title vacant: Holmes vacated the title after a dispute with his promoter Don King over the proposed purse for a fight against mandatory challenger Greg Page.
Mike Tyson regains the title (def. Frank Bruno)
Title vacant: Tyson vacated the title to pursue a bout against Evander Holyfield instead of mandatory challenger Lennox Lewis.
Lennox Lewis regains the title (def. Oliver McCall for the vacant title)
Lennox Lewis regains the title (def. Hasim Rahman)
Title vacant: Lewis retired as champion and chose not to rematch Vitali Klitschko ahead of a WBC-mandated 1 March deadline to accept the bout.
Hasim Rahman regains the title (interim champion promoted)
Vitali Klitschko regains the title (def. Samuel Peter)
Oleksandr Usyk wins the title (def. Tyson Fury) and holds it at the end of 2025
